info.educationalGoals: In this course, we will build a full compiler. We will spend a little bit of time on parsing, but most of the time on how to actually transform code from a high-level language into an equivalent program in x86. By the end of the course, you should be able to actually build small compiler entirely on your own, and could help in developing large open-source compilers.
info.description: This course covers the key components of a compiler for a high level programming language. Topics include lexical analysis, parsing, type checking, code generation and optimization. Students will work in teams to design and implement an actual compiler making use of tools such as lex and yacc.
info.title: Principles of Compiler Design

Students requiring accommodations as a result of a disability can contact the Centre for Accessible Learning (caladmin@sfu.ca).
